bullets.title: Fed Warsh hawkish debut: hike risk is live, market pricing ~40-50bp in 2026
bullets.body: New Fed Chair Warsh's first FOMC meeting was perceived as a hawkish pivot — core PCE forecasts raised to 3.3% for 2026, dovish language stripped from the statement, and forward guidance shortened. BofA expects three 25bp hikes (Sept/Oct/Dec); Deutsche Bank 50bp total; markets pricing ~42bp. The key threshold: core PCE must print ≤0.21%/month to avoid hikes; it's running ~0.36% this year. MS chief economist Gapen sees Fed on hold through year-end, while GS cuts US recession risk to 15% from 25%. If inflation undershoots the Fed's 3.3% forecast (MS base case: 3.0%), markets may have over-priced tightening.

bullets.title: Macro backdrop: nominal GDP solid at 5.3%; lower oil boosts consumer confidence
bullets.body: Multiple strategists highlight nominal GDP running 5.5-6% (5.3% 4Q avg), with fed funds at 3.6% already stimulative. Consumer and CEO confidence rebounding sharply — Business Roundtable CEO survey at highest since 4Q24 (72% correlation to real GDP). Gasoline price declines driving a confidence spike in low-end consumers. Core goods inflation at 0.4% (6M annualized); headline disinflation accelerating. Base case for real GDP growth ~3%, with upside from fiscal capex expensing and AI productivity.

bullets.title: US-Iran peace deal reduces oil tail risk; WTI targets $70-80 range
bullets.body: US and Iran agreed on a 60-day roadmap in Switzerland, including oil sanction waivers and naval blockade lift. Strait of Hormuz disruption proved brief — 17M barrels and 55 ships transited Saturday. WTI fell ~1.6% to $75 on the news; long-dated futures below $70 signal durable supply headwind. Roth upgraded oil E&P stocks (APA, COP, FANG et al.) after 15-22% declines, seeing stabilization ~$75/bbl. GS expects Brent ~$80 by YE2026; MS sees crude back to $90. Airlines a beneficiary; oil-exposed EM LatAm faces rate-cut headwinds as inflation relief insufficient for policy shifts.

bullets.title: Equity positioning at seasonal peak; HFs net selling but gross leverage still elevated
bullets.body: JPM and GS prime data show hedge funds net-sold 5 of past 6 days (US-led), strongest in Tech, Industrials, Materials — recent top performers. Gross leverage buildup unusually large (May +22% vs 6% avg; June +18% vs 10% avg), typically peaks mid-June post-expiry and declines ~5%. US Tactical Positioning Monitor moved back to ~+1z from -2z. Yet US equities attracted a record $119.2B inflow for week ended 6/17 (tech record $19.2B). SPX logged 11th up week in 12; Dow and RTY at new ATHs. Retail continues buying via ETFs, offsetting HF net selling.

bullets.title: Memory supercycle: DRAM/NAND ASPs surging 40-50% in 3Q, MU earnings Wed the key AI read
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side desks converge: memory contract prices up 40-50% q/q in 3Q26 and 30-40% in 4Q26 per memory consultant. Morgan Stanley models DRAM ASPs +45% q/q, NAND +50%; Jefferies sees ~$200 MU EPS for CY27 with $30 in August print. GS estimates MU F3Q revs ~$48.7bn, EPS ~$29.95 vs street $23.70 — ~20%+ above consensus. Key focus: SCA announcements (~75% of buyside expects additional SCAs at 30-50% forward bit coverage), HBM pricing, and 2027 capacity commentary. Memory stocks (MU, WDC, SNDK) up 4-6% pre-market Monday; SK Hynix surpassed Samsung in Korean market cap; Hynix Nasdaq ADR listing expected as early as August.

bullets.title: Price Momentum at 97th percentile vs EPS Momentum — catch-up trade favored
bullets.body: The NTM P/E premium of top-decile Price Momentum stocks vs. EPS Momentum reached the 97th percentile, signaling stretched relative valuation. 22V Research and Morgan Stanley strategy both flag EPS Momentum as offering better risk-reward from here. GARP basket up 15.6% YTD. Fed tightening scenario (ERP rising from 4.6% toward 5%) implies -9% downside to fair value on the price momentum basket; EPS Momentum expected to outperform in a catch-up trade as AI broadens into chemicals and materials.

bullets.title: ACN crashes 24% on bookings miss — AI disruption fear spreads to IT Services
bullets.body: Accenture reported FY3Q26 bookings -3% cc, missing Visible Alpha consensus by 7%; cut FY26 revenue growth guidance to 3-4% from 3-5%. Stock fell ~24% last week (largest single-day drop on record). TD Cowen cut ACN to Hold from Buy, PT $150 from $258. UBS interprets as AI disintermediation risk for IT services broadly. European peers (Capgemini) face pressure; UBS prefers to be underweight hyperscalers/software and overweight memory/optical/HDD supply chain. One MS analyst stays Buy at $275 PT, viewing as positioning dislocation.

bullets.title: Semis +113% YTD; tech sector breadth narrowing, raising fragility risk
bullets.body: Semiconductor sector is up 113% YTD (Jefferies), with MU responsible for 17% of S&P 500 YTD gains and the top-10 stocks driving 83% of S&P returns. CRDO up 858%, MU up 692%, ALAB up 560% over two years. JPM strategist warns the chip rally poses a market-tangle risk — narrowing breadth, rising correlations, and leveraged ETF usage increase fragility. 2026 has seen more 5% momentum moves in semis than the prior 8 years combined. S&P index changes effective 6/22: MRVL and FLEX added to S&P 500.

bullets.title: AI power infrastructure buildout accelerating; MSFT-Chevron 20-year, 2.67 GW deal signed
bullets.body: Chevron subsidiary Energy Forge One signed a 20-year PPA with Microsoft for Project Kilby in West Texas — ~2.67 GW capacity, majority via GE Vernova turbines, FID by end-2026, first power 2028, targeting mid-teen returns. FERC issued orders requiring grid operators to reform large-load interconnection, supporting BTM generation. BKR observing no available manufacturing slots until 2029; global power demand expected +4.2% CAGR over 15 years with $1.6tn data center/AI infrastructure spend by 2030. ABC data center contractors report 11.6-month construction backlogs vs 8.6 months for non-DC exposure.

bullets.title: Warsh's Fed: reducing forward guidance is the key structural shift
bullets.body: Multiple research notes flag Warsh's communications overhaul as the most lasting change — shorter post-meeting statement, elimination of dovish language, reduced forward guidance echoing pre-1994 era. This could lift US borrowing costs and boost volatility structurally. Fed is also studying balance sheet changes (Treasury account reduction, duration removal via QT). S&P 500/Gold ratio up ~40% since Warsh nomination, suggesting market reads the change as credibility-building, not credibility-damaging. Near-term equity headwind from liquidity tightening (RMP down 75% from peak) heading into July.

bullets.title: UBS/GS strategy: rotate from crowded AI complex into US cyclicals, financials
bullets.body: UBS European strategy notes hedge funds reducing crowded AI capex positions (US tech, semis, power, capital goods) and recycling into US cyclicals, industrials, and financials. GS prime data confirm Info Tech, Industrials, and Utilities were most net-sold last week while Financials, Materials, Energy led net buys. Fed CCAR results expected June 24 seen as a near-term catalyst to refocus investors on banks, which are up only 2.7% YTD despite an 8.1% rally last month and their first lighter regulatory environment in 20+ years. JPM clients also rotating: reducing Europe, adding Asia/Korea/China.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 up 20.1% YTD, outperforming S&P by 10.5%; earnings tracking below but revenues ahead
bullets.body: Russell 2000 surged 2.1% on June 18, outperforming the S&P 500 by 1.0%. YTD the index is up 20.1%, outperforming the S&P 500 by 10.5%, with S&P 600 up 18.8%. Of 1,127 R2K companies that have reported 1Q26, aggregate earnings track 12.7% below expectations, but revenues lead by 2.6%. Tech, Industrials, and Discretionary are the top-performing R2K sectors YTD.

bullets.title: AI equity financing revival: share issuance could overtake buybacks for first time in 23 years
bullets.body: Goldman projects US share issuance to reach 1.8% of aggregate market cap in 2026 (up from 0.6% prior year), potentially exceeding buybacks (2.0%) for the first time since 2003. Alphabet announced an $84.7B equity financing plan; Oracle planning $40B; Meta considering stock offering. SpaceX IPO seen as the signal event — but analysts warn current conditions (transformative tech, excess liquidity, retail fervor) fit bubble hallmarks. The number of listed US firms has fallen to 3,908 from 8,090 in 1996.

bullets.title: FOXA-ROKU deal: Fox down 20%, deal underwhelms; NFLX withdrew from bidding
bullets.body: Fox agreed to acquire Roku at ~22x FY27E EBITDA (vs Fox's own 8x pre-deal), levering to 2.8x net. FOXA stock fell 20%+ post-announcement. NFLX withdrew from bidding per Semafor. Fox pro-forma trades 7.8x NTM EV/EBITDA within its 2-year historical range. FOXA 2026 upfront commitments grew HSD% with Tubi and Fox News both showing double-digit growth. Investors skeptical about Roku revenue growth decelerating in FY27 unless Home Screen Initiative drives material gains. Deal expected to close H1 2027.

bullets.title: China rare earth export controls on US firms; COHR CEO in Beijing lobbying for InP access
bullets.body: China added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export control list. Critical minerals (gallium, germanium, indium phosphide) are gating factors for US data center buildout. Trump included the Coherent CEO in the Beijing delegation to lobby for indium phosphide access. China accounts for ~28% of US AI-related imports (adjusted for rerouting) despite a $156B deficit in advanced compute. Trump administration has imposed no new export controls on Chinese firms since October — longest stretch in years — maintaining a supply-chain truce.

bullets.title: Software value shifting: 'good sticky' platforms (SNOW, PLTR, SAP) vs. AI-disrupted vendors (CRM down 13 days)
bullets.body: SAP CEO warns AI 'vibe coding' could remove human developers within 3-4 years; PE firms now use vibecoding to test software defensibility. Software value accruing to platforms with open data standards, governed single source of truth, and custom agentic apps — SNOW, PLTR, MSFT, NOW, SAP named as beneficiaries. SNOW confirmed AI pass-through revenues are immaterial (~1% of mix), making its ~30%+ reported growth 'clean' vs Databricks' 15-point boost from model reselling. CRM is down 13 consecutive days (~27% decline), longest losing streak ever. Security software (PANW, CRWD) trading at 65% premium to Software vs 30% a year ago.

bullets.title: UK PM Starmer resigns; Andy Burnham likely successor by July-September
bullets.body: UK PM Keir Starmer is preparing to resign; Burnham allies are confident of succession by September. The political transition introduces uncertainty for UK markets. JPM option hedges include MCX < UKX positioning on UK political risk. European equities broadly mixed Monday morning (FTSE +0.27%, DAX -0.26%, CAC -0.65%).

bullets.title: QCOM Analyst Day Wednesday: data center diversification story tests re-rating
bullets.body: QCOM Investor Day Wednesday is viewed as a test of whether the market will re-rate the stock from handset cyclicality toward AI/data center diversification. UBS estimates QCOM could reach ~$70B revenues and $20+ EPS by FY31, with data center/AI contributing ~$20B. QCOM reportedly in talks to acquire Tenstorrent for ~$8-10B to balance decode/prefill AI inference workloads. Automotive business on track for $8B FY29 target; combined non-handset revenue opportunity ~$25B by FY31.

bullets.title: Personal saving rate at 2.6% defensible given household net worth near record highs
bullets.body: The personal saving rate fell to 2.6% in April, only 70bps above pre-GFC lows. However, household net worth-to-PDI rebounded near Q1 2022 record highs, with asset price revaluation over 8 quarters raising net worth by ~80% of current PDI. The wealth effect of ~4 cents per dollar from asset appreciation explains the ~3 percentage point decline in saving rate, suggesting the low savings rate is not anomalously alarming.

bullets.title: Iran nuclear talks: mid-stage, not late-stage; hardliners retain advantage on both sides
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag US-Iran talks in Switzerland as resembling mid-stage rather than late-stage negotiation. Washington has not yet fully aligned with Israel or closed internal debates. Hardliners in both the US and Iran retain negotiating advantage; Trump's political capital and 2026 midterm calculus may be determinative. US intelligence remains skeptical a full nuclear deal will finalize. Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire effective June 19, with Israeli troops remaining in Lebanese security zone.
